slides.headline: THE 5 PROMPTS THAT STOP CLAUDE FROM QUITTING HALFWAY THROUGH YOUR JOB
slides.kicker: Claude stops mid-task and calls it done

slides.headline: 1) THE ONLY LINE CLAUDE NEVER IGNORES
slides.body:
Claude quits long tasks halfway and calls them complete. Claude treats the contract as a hard rule.

"Your job is not done until I have every section in full. Start now."

slides.headline: 2) BREAK THE TASK INTO SIGNED-OFF CHUNKS
slides.body:
One sub-task at a time stops Claude drifting. Use this.

"Complete ONLY this one step, then stop and write: 'Step complete. Ready for the next?'

Step: [paste exactly one sub-task]"

slides.headline: 3) RESET CLAUDE WITHOUT STARTING OVER
slides.body: This one line costs 15 seconds. Claude picks up mid-sentence without losing context. "You stopped before finishing. Here is your last output: [paste it]. Continue from that exact point. Do not repeat anything."

slides.headline: 4) GIVE CLAUDE A JOB TITLE WITH STAKES
slides.body:
Role framing alone changes how Claude handles gaps.

"You are a senior [role]. This work will be reviewed by a client. Your task: [the job]. Do not stop until complete. Do it."

slides.headline: 5) RUN THE SELF-AUDIT LOOP
slides.body:
Claude marks tasks complete when parts are missing. Run this after any long output.

"Review your last response. Mark each item: COMPLETE, PARTIAL, or NOT DONE. Complete anything incomplete. Do not ask permission."

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: 5 PROMPTS THAT FINISH THE JOB
slides.body:
1) The completion contract
2) Signed-off chunks
3) Reset without starting over
4) Job title with stakes
5) Self-audit loop

caption:
Swipe for 5 copy-paste prompts that stop Claude from quitting halfway, looping back, or delivering half a job and calling it done. 🔧

Completion contract that defines done before the task starts, signed-off chunk method that checkpoints every sub-task so Claude cannot drift, the exact reset prompt that picks up mid-task without losing context, job-title-with-stakes setup that raises effort on long deliverables, self-audit loop that makes Claude check and complete its own gaps.

A post with 2.5 million views surfaced a real problem: Claude quits long tasks halfway and most people just re-prompt. The fix is in the opening line. These five prompts give Claude a clear definition of done. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we will show you what this could do for yours.
